text.en: Recite the poem in a happy voice, an angry voice and a surprised voice.

Let us Listen: sit in a circle and give five rhyming words for each word: ship, tree, bow, rain, sun, sea, sail, and, sky, far. Focus on sound and not spelling.
Let us Speak: recite short poems such as Colours (about sharing crayons) and Aachoo! (an elephant with a cold) in different voices. Think about gestures and expressions and about which feeling the reciter is conveying.
Let us Write: write a paragraph of 80 to 100 words about a journey to a place you visited recently. Say the time and destination, the purpose, whom you travelled with, what you liked or disliked, local food, and a monument or scenery. Use the past tense.
Compound words: a word joins a friend word to make a new one, such as rain plus bow gives rainbow, tea plus cup gives teacup, note plus book gives notebook, and sun plus flower gives sunflower.
Other poem activities: find rhyming pairs, find repeated words, give a new title, and say which musical instrument you would use to read the poem.
